en: Abdullah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Darimi narrated to us, Abu al-Yaman informed us, Shu'ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri, Abu Salamah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to me, that 'A'ishah, wife of the Prophet (pbuh), said: The Messenger of Allah (pbuh) said: "O 'A'ish, here is Gabriel greeting you with salam." She said: So I said, "And upon him be peace and the mercy of Allah." She said: And he sees what I do not see.
And Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated it to us, Asbat ibn Muhammad informed us, from Zakariyya', with this chain of narration, the like of it.

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated it to us, al-Mula'i informed us, Zakariyya' ibn Abi Za'idah narrated to us, he said: I heard 'Amir saying: Abu Salamah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to me that 'A'ishah narrated to him that the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) said to her... with the like of the hadith of both of them.

And Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, 'Abd al-Rahim ibn Sulayman and Ya'la ibn 'Ubayd narrated to us, from Zakariyya', from al-Sha'bi, from Abu Salamah, from 'A'ishah, that she narrated to him that the Prophet (pbuh) said to her: "Indeed Gabriel greets you with salam." She said: So I said, "And upon him be peace and the mercy of Allah."

Yahya ibn Yahya, Qutaybah, and Ibn Hujr narrated to us—they said: Isma'il—meaning Ibn Ja'far—narrated to us; (H) and Qutaybah narrated to us, 'Abd al-'Aziz—meaning Ibn Muhammad—narrated to us—both of them from 'Abdullah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from Anas, from the Prophet (pbuh), the like of it. And in neither of their hadiths is "I heard the Messenger of Allah (pbuh)." And in the hadith of Isma'il, he heard Anas ibn Malik.

Abdullah ibn Maslamah ibn Qa'nab narrated to us, Sulayman—meaning Ibn Bilal—narrated to us, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) saying: "The superiority of 'A'ishah over other women is like the superiority of tharid over all other food."

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Hanzali narrated to us, and 'Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us, both from Abu Nu'aym—'Abd said: Abu Nu'aym narrated to us—'Abd al-Wahid ibn Ayman narrated to us, Ibn Abi Mulaykah narrated to me, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from 'A'ishah, who said: Whenever the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) intended to go out on a journey, he would cast lots among his wives, and the lot fell to 'A'ishah and Hafsah, so both of them went out with him together. At night, the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) would travel alongside 'A'ishah and converse with her. Hafsah said to 'A'ishah: "Will you not ride my camel tonight and I ride your camel, so that you see and I see?" She said: "Yes." So 'A'ishah rode upon Hafsah's camel, and Hafsah rode upon 'A'ishah's camel. The Messenger of Allah (pbuh) came up to 'A'ishah's camel while Hafsah was upon it, greeted her with salam, and then travelled alongside her until they encamped. 'A'ishah missed his company and felt jealous. When they encamped, she began putting her foot among the idhkhir grass, saying: "O Lord, unleash a scorpion or a snake upon me to bite me; it is Your Messenger, and I cannot say anything to him."

Abd al-Malik ibn Shu'ayb ibn al-Layth ibn Sa'd narrated to me, my father narrated to me, from my grandfather, 'Uqayl ibn Khalid narrated to me, he said: Ibn Shihab said: Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab and 'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr informed me among men of knowledge that 'A'ishah, the wife of the Prophet (pbuh), said: The Messenger of Allah (pbuh) used to say while he was healthy: "Never has a prophet been taken until he sees his seat in Paradise, and then he is given the choice." 'A'ishah said: When death descended upon the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) while his head was on my thigh, he fainted for a while, then regained consciousness and fixed his gaze toward the ceiling, then said: "O Allah, the Exalted Companionship." 'A'ishah said: I said, "Then he does not choose us." 'A'ishah said: And I recognized the statement that he used to narrate to us while he was healthy, in his saying: "Never has a prophet been taken until he sees his seat in Paradise, and then he is given the choice." 'A'ishah said: So that was the last statement the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) spoke—his saying: "O Allah, the Exalted Companionship."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated it to us, Waki' narrated to us; (H) and 'Ubaydullah ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, my father narrated to us—they said: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Sa'd, with this chain of narration, the like of it.

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashshar both narrated to us—and the wording is Ibn al-Muthanna's—they said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Sa'd ibn Ibrahim, from 'Urwah, from 'A'ishah, who said: I used to hear that no prophet would ever die until he was given the choice between this world and the Hereafter. She said: Then I heard the Prophet (pbuh) during his illness in which he died, hoarseness having overcome his voice, saying: "With those upon whom Allah has bestowed favor of the prophets, the steadfast affirmers of truth, the martyrs, and the righteous; and excellent are those as companions." She said: So I knew that he had been given the choice at that moment.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Abu Kurayb both narrated to us—they said: Abu Usamah narrated to us; (H) and Ibn Numayr narrated to us, my father narrated to us; (H) and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, 'Abdah ibn Sulayman informed us—all of them from Hisham, with this chain of narration, the like of it.

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from Malik ibn Anas, regarding what was read to him, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from 'Abbad ibn 'Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr, from 'A'ishah, that she informed him that she heard the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) saying before he died, while he was leaning against her chest and she was listening intently to him while he was saying: "O Allah, forgive me and have mercy upon me, and join me with the Exalted Companionship."

And Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, he said: I found in my book, from Abu Usamah, from Hisham, from his father, from 'A'ishah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (pbuh) would inquire, saying: "Where am I today? Where am I tomorrow?" longing for the day of 'A'ishah. She said: When my day arrived, Allah took his soul between my chest and neck.

Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah ibn Qahzad narrated it to me, he said: 'Abdullah ibn 'Uthman narrated it to me, from 'Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak, from Yunus, from al-Zuhri, with this chain of narration, the like of it in meaning, except that he said: "When I turned upon her, I did not cease until I subdued her completely in victory."

Al-Hasan ibn 'Ali al-Hulwani, Abu Bakr ibn al-Nadr, and 'Abd ibn Humayd narrated to me—'Abd said: narrated to me, and the other two said: Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim ibn Sa'd narrated to us—my father narrated to me, from Salih, from Ibn Shihab, Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Harith ibn Hisham informed me that 'A'ishah, the wife of the Prophet (pbuh), said: The wives of the Prophet (pbuh) sent Fatimah, daughter of the Messenger of Allah (pbuh), to the Messenger of Allah (pbuh). She asked permission to enter while he was lying with me under my woolen blanket, and he granted her permission. She said: "O Messenger of Allah, your wives have sent me to you asking of you justice regarding the daughter of Abu Quhafah," while I remained silent. She said: The Messenger of Allah (pbuh) said to her: "O my little daughter, do you not love what I love?" She said: "Yes." He said: "Then love this one." She said: Fatimah stood up upon hearing that from the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) and returned to the wives of the Prophet (pbuh) and informed them of what she had said and what the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) had said to her. They said to her: "We do not see that you have availed us in anything, so return to the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) and say to him: 'Your wives adjure you by Allah for justice regarding the daughter of Abu Quhafah.'" Fatimah said: "By Allah, I will never speak to him concerning her again." 'A'ishah said: Then the wives of the Prophet (pbuh) sent Zaynab bint Jahsh, wife of the Prophet (pbuh)—and she was the one who rivaled me among them in status with the Messenger of Allah (pbuh), and I never saw any woman better in religion than Zaynab, more godfearing, more truthful in speech, more observant of family ties, greater in charity, or more self-sacrificing in deeds by which she gave charity and drew closer to Allah, exalted be He, except for a quickness of temper that was in her from which she was swift to return to composure. She said: She asked permission to enter upon the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) while the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) was with 'A'ishah in her woolen blanket in the same state in which Fatimah had entered upon him. The Messenger of Allah (pbuh) granted her permission, and she said: "O Messenger of Allah, your wives have sent me to you asking of you justice regarding the daughter of Abu Quhafah." She said: Then she fell upon me, speaking harshly and reviling me, while I kept watching the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) and watching his eyes to see whether he would permit me to respond to her. She said: Zaynab did not desist until I knew that the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) would not dislike it if I defended myself. She said: So when I turned upon her, I did not let up until I overpowered her completely. She said: The Messenger of Allah (pbuh) smiled and said: "She is indeed the daughter of Abu Bakr."

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, 'Abdah narrated to us, from Hisham, from his father, from 'A'ishah, that the people used to choose the day of 'A'ishah to send their gifts, seeking thereby the pleasure of the Messenger of Allah (pbuh).

Abu Kurayb narrated it to us, Abu Usamah narrated to us; (H) and Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to us, Jarir narrated to us; (H) and Ibn Numayr narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Bishr narrated to us—all of them from Hisham, with this chain of narration. And in the hadith of Jarir he said: "I used to play with the dolls in his house, and they are toys."

Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us, 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Muhammad informed us, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father, from 'A'ishah, that she used to play with dolls in the presence of the Messenger of Allah (pbuh). She said: And my girl companions would come to me, and they would withdraw in bashfulness from the Messenger of Allah (pbuh). She said: So the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) would usher them in to me.
And Ibn Numayr narrated it to us, 'Abdah narrated to us, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, with this chain of narration up to his saying: "No, by the Lord of Ibrahim." And he did not mention what was after it.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, he said: I found in my book, from Abu Usamah, Hisham narrated to us; (H) and Abu Kurayb Muhammad ibn al-'Ala' narrated to us, Abu Usamah narrated to us, from Hisham, from his father, from 'A'ishah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (pbuh) said to me: "Indeed, I surely know when you are pleased with me and when you are angry with me." She said: I said, "And from where do you know that?" He said: "When you are pleased with me, you say: 'No, by the Lord of Muhammad.' But when you are angry with me, you say: 'No, by the Lord of Ibrahim.'" She said: I said, "Yes, by Allah, O Messenger of Allah, I do not leave aside except your name."
Ibn Numayr narrated to us, Ibn Idris narrated to us; (H) and Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Abu Usamah narrated to us—both of them from Hisham, with this chain of narration, similarly.

Khalaf ibn Hisham and Abu al-Rabi' both narrated to us from Hammad ibn Zayd—and the wording is Abu al-Rabi's—Hammad narrated to us, Hisham narrated to us, from his father, from 'A'ishah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (pbuh) said: "You were shown to me in a dream for three nights: the angel brought you to me wrapped in a piece of silk, saying: 'This is your wife.' So I uncovered your face, and behold, it was you! I said: 'If this is from Allah, He will bring it to pass.'"

Suwayd ibn Sa'id narrated to us, 'Ali ibn Mushir narrated to us, from Hisham, from his father, from 'A'ishah, who said: Halah bint Khuwaylid, sister of Khadijah, sought permission to enter upon the Messenger of Allah (pbuh), and he recognized Khadijah's manner of seeking permission, which brought him comfort and gladness. He said: "O Allah, Halah bint Khuwaylid!" So I became jealous and said: "Why do you remember an old woman from among the old women of Quraysh, red-gummed, who died long ago in time, when Allah has replaced her for you with someone better than her?"

Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us, 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from 'Urwah, from 'A'ishah, who said: The Prophet (pbuh) did not marry another woman while Khadijah was alive until she died.

Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us, 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from 'Urwah, from 'A'ishah, who said: I never felt jealous toward any of the wives of the Prophet (pbuh) as I felt jealous toward Khadijah, because of his frequent mention of her, though I never saw her at all.

Zuhayr ibn Harb and Abu Kurayb both narrated to us from Abu Mu'awiyah, Hisham narrated to us, with this chain of narration, similar to the hadith of Abu Usamah up to the story of the sheep, and he did not mention the addition after it.

Sahl ibn 'Uthman narrated to us, Hafs ibn Ghiyath narrated to us, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father, from 'A'ishah, who said: I never felt jealous of any of the wives of the Prophet (pbuh) except Khadijah, though I did not live during her time. She said: Whenever the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) slaughtered a sheep, he would say: "Send portions of it to the friends of Khadijah." She said: One day I angered him and said: "Khadijah?!" Thereupon the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) said: "Indeed, I was nourished with her love."

Abu Kurayb Muhammad ibn al-'Ala' narrated to us, Abu Usamah narrated to us, Hisham narrated to us, from his father, from 'A'ishah, who said: I never felt jealous toward any woman as I felt jealous toward Khadijah—and she had passed away three years before he married me—because of what I used to hear him mentioning her. And her Lord, Mighty and Majestic, had commanded him to give her the glad tidings of a palace made of reeds in Paradise; and whenever he slaughtered a sheep, he would send gifts of it to her intimate friends.

Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, 'Abdah narrated to us, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father, from 'A'ishah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (pbuh) gave glad tidings to Khadijah bint Khuwaylid of a house in Paradise.

Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us, Abu Mu'awiyah informed us; (H) and Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, Waki' narrated to us; (H) and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, al-Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman and Jarir informed us; (H) and Ibn Abi 'Umar narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us—all of them from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from Ibn Abi Awfa, from the Prophet (pbuh), the like of it.
